variants.name: Inja template engine (C++17, header-only)
variants.implementation_notes: Inja is the modern default: include inja.hpp, keep one inja::Environment that holds the parsed templates, and render against a nlohmann::json model (env.render_file(path, data)); call env.set_html_autoescape(true) for HTML output, since escaping is not on unless the environment is told to escape. Choose it when the toolchain is C++17 or later and templates are edited outside the build.
pitfalls: Templates are parsed on the request path: an unknown variable or a syntax error raises inja::RenderError at render time, so parse every template at startup as a smoke check.
set_html_autoescape(true) is a per-environment switch; a second environment for XML/CSV output must not inherit the HTML escaping assumption.

variants.name: kainjow/Mustache logic-less templates (C++11)
variants.implementation_notes: kainjow/Mustache is a header-only C++11 realization: build a mustache::data model (sections are lists, holes are strings) and render a template string or file with mustache::mustache, which escapes by default. Logic-less means every condition and iteration is expressed as a section ({{#rows}}...{{/rows}}) and every computed value has to be precomputed into the model - the right trade when the toolchain predates C++17 or when the team wants templates that cannot grow logic.
pitfalls: Sections have no comparison operators: a predicate that is not precomputed in C++ silently renders the wrong branch instead of failing.
Section iteration is positional; a model whose list order differs from the intended page order is a presentation bug with no compile-time symptom.
